cohort: The study included 1,172,546 Norwegian deliveries between 1995 and 2014, analyzed by municipality of residence.
finding: Most adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes (perineal tears, neonatal encephalopathy, cerebral palsy, stillbirths) were least frequent in municipalities with caesarean rates above 15%, though lower rates were associated with less frequent maternal haemorrhage.
mod_finding: A local caesarean-delivery rate of 10% was associated with nearly a two-fold risk of neonatal encephalopathy and a 50% higher occurrence of cerebral palsy compared with areas with a caesarean-delivery rate of 20%, while lower rates were associated with less frequent maternal haemorrhage.
